The accept family for $\alpha$ at bounds $T$ and $H$ is the CNF formula formed by the accept-code clauses at $T$ and $H$ followed by the accept-cell clauses for $\alpha$ at $T$ and $H$.

nodes.summary: A configuration $c$ of a finite stack machine $M$ is accepting for a symbol $\alpha$ of the output stack of $M$ when $c$ is halted (it has no label), its state is the initial state of $M$, and the output stack of $c$ is nonempty with top symbol $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Accepting configuration

nodes.summary: For an encoding $E$ of a finite stack machine $M$, the accepting code is the (label, state) code that $E$ assigns to the pair of the halted label and the initial state of $M$, the label and state of a halted configuration as acceptance reads it.
nodes.title: Accepting code

nodes.summary: Let $V \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\ell$ be a list of pairs $(p, b)$ of a variable index $p$ and a sign $b$ that is faithful for $V$, and let $a$ be a list of Booleans. Then $a$ satisfies the dense clause over $V$ variables built from $\ell$ if and only if some $(p, b) \in \ell$ has $p < |a|$ and $a_p = b$.
nodes.title: Exact clause semantics

nodes.summary: A list $\ell$ of literals $(p, b)$, each a variable index $p \in \mathbb{N}$ with a sign $b$, is faithful for $V \in \mathbb{N}$ when every literal $(p, b)$ of $\ell$ has $p < V$ and the first literal of $\ell$ with index $p$ is $(p, b)$.
nodes.title: Faithful literal list

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is a faithful family over $V$ variables when every clause of $\varphi$ is the dense clause over $V$ variables built from some list of literals that is faithful for $V$.
nodes.title: Faithful dense clause family

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is a faithful family with positive literals over $V$ variables when every clause of $\varphi$ is the dense clause over $V$ variables built from some list $\ell$ of literals that is faithful for $V$ and contains a positive literal $(p, \mathrm{true})$ for some $p$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
